features.title: A branch is dragged on the canvas, and a node can be removed
features.user_visible_behavior: Dragging from a node's output port to another node's input port points that node at a new parent, and a control on the node removes it, reconnecting its children to its parent. A connection that would make a cycle does not drop, and says why.
verification: cd frontend && npx vitest run - the graph rules in edits.ts, including every refusal.
cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/pipeline.spec.ts - the drag and the removal in a browser.
features.evidence: 2026-08-29. `npx vitest run` - 10 files, 77 tests passed, including src/__tests__/edits.test.ts (14 tests: connect replaces the target's input, a fork gives one node two children, cycle/self/source-target/duplicate/unknown are refused, removal reconnects every child, the source is refused). `npx playwright test` - 38 passed across all four projects, including the four new cases in e2e/pipeline.spec.ts: msc->centre_a rewires and the edge count stays 13, pca_a->snv is refused with 'would make a cycle' and no edge appears, removing snv leaves source->centre_a and source->snv_savgol with 13 nodes, and the source node carries no remove control. `npx tsc -b --noEmit` and `npx eslint .` both exit 0.
features.notes: Items 1 and 4 of #51. The rules live in frontend/src/canvas/edits.ts, pure and tested, and are enforced during the drag through React Flow's isValidConnection - each refusal is the client half of a models.py validator. Every non-source node holds exactly one input (tuple[NodeId]), so connecting replaces rather than appends and a branch is one node with several children; an edge cannot be cut on its own because the child would be left dangling. The remove control is on the node rather than in the side panel: clicking a node opens its tab, which replaces the panel before it could be used. Edits are held locally and saved by the existing whole-list PUT (#108). Node positions are still not draggable - layout lives in pipeline_state.json and nothing writes it back.

features.title: Duplicate a subgraph, and compare two terminal nodes in one tab
features.user_visible_behavior: A subgraph can be duplicated so a variant is built from an existing path rather than from scratch, and selecting two terminal nodes opens a tab comparing their results.
verification: The duplicate produces an independent branch with fresh node ids, asserted in the browser.
Two terminal nodes open one comparison tab showing both models' metrics.
features.notes: Items 2 and 3 of #51, deliberately left for a second pass. The comparison tab is a screen with no artboard behind it and no metrics to compare until PLS has a kernel in the executor (#88's subject), which is what makes 'compare two models' worth looking at. DESIGN_BRIEF.md section 5 is the reference.
